issues.title: False pointwise fractional product rule
issues.failure_explanation: Take α=2 and f=g=2+cos(x_1), independent of x_2. At x_1=π, f=g=1, (-Δ)f=(-Δ)g=-1, and (-Δ)(fg)=-2. Since C(2)=2, the asserted inequality becomes -2≤2(-1-1)=-4, which is false. Consequently, the pointwise decomposition used in est_nonl cannot justify the local high-Sobolev estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform nonlinear energy estimate establishing bd3 is unsupported, so the local Galerkin convergence and the formal results that use that bound are not established by the old proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the false pointwise rule and replace it with valid periodic Kato–Ponce product and commutator estimates. In the Galerkin energy argument, use Λ^s(u∂₁u)=u∂₁Λ^s u+[Λ^s,u]∂₁u; integration by parts and H^s embedding into W^{1,∞} then give d‖u_N‖_s²/dt≤C‖u_N‖_s³ with C independent of N. Take s≥1+α and s>2, so the α=1 endpoint requires slightly more than H² regularity, and propagate this corrected regularity through conv_lemma, thm:exisuq, and thm:spectral_accuracy.
issues.why_classification: The displayed pointwise assertion has a smooth counterexample and the proof uses its false decomposition, so this is not transcriptional. A valid repair requires a new commutator lemma and a reworked nonlinear energy estimate, with a limited strengthening at the natural α=1 endpoint. That work is nontrivial but contained and does not require global proof reconstruction.

issues.title: Invalid continuation to global well-posedness

failure_location.quote: Since the semi-discrete approximation is bounded on the $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}$-norm uniformly in time \eqref{bd3}, we may repeatedly apply the local existence and uniqueness Lemma \ref{conv_lemma}.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then there exists a finite time $\bar T$ such that the following bounds hold

issues.failure_explanation: For α in [1,2] and initial data in H^{1+α}, thm:exisuq claims existence and uniqueness on every finite interval. The argument establishes a bound only through a lifespan bar T determined by the current high Sobolev norm. At a restart, that norm and hence the next lifespan may change; no uniform lower bound for successive lifespans or all-time H^{1+α} estimate is established. Thus the local construction does not support the global theorem.
issues.overall_effect: Global strong well-posedness is unproved, and the later spectral proof cannot use bd3 with an N-independent constant on an arbitrary interval without an independent high-norm bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: The least source-supported complete repair is to replace thm:exisuq by a local-in-time strong well-posedness theorem on the uniform lifespan established by conv_lemma, delete the iterative global-continuation claim, and restrict Galerkin and spectral conclusions to that lifespan or to intervals on which an independent uniform high-Sobolev bound is explicitly assumed. Corresponding all-time claims in the surrounding text must also be withdrawn.
issues.why_classification: The old estimate holds only up to a norm-dependent lifespan, and restarting supplies neither a uniform lower bound on successive lifespans nor an all-time high-norm estimate. Downgrading global strong well-posedness to a local or conditional result is major mathematical loss, while retaining the all-time theorem would require a new global a priori mechanism or proof architecture not established in the source.

issues.title: Invalid W1-infinity estimate in the spectral-convergence proof
issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the L∞ norm of a first derivative of the modified projection by H^2 seminorms. On the two-dimensional torus, H^2 does not embed into W^{1,∞}; one needs H^μ with μ>2. In particular, α=1 and r=2 satisfy the old theorem's assumptions but provide no such μ. The analogous use of bd3 to make the coefficient involving ∂_{x_1}u_N independent of N has the same endpoint problem. Hence the Grönwall coefficient and the claimed uniform N^{-r} estimate are not established throughout the stated range.
issues.overall_effect: The algebraic spectral rate is unproved under the theorem's low-regularity range, especially at α=1, r=2; the later fully discrete prose cannot rely on that spatial estimate in this regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the nonlinear error difference so that its quadratic coefficient is ∂₁ of the modified projection rather than ∂₁u_N; in particular, its pairing with the error reduces to a multiple of (∂₁ of the modified projection, E_N²). Impose r≥α+1 together with r>2, choose 2<μ<r, and use the modified-projection estimate in H^μ and the embedding H^μ into W^{1,∞} to obtain an N-independent coefficient. This preserves the N^{-r} rate but excludes the α=1, r=2 endpoint unless a separate endpoint estimate is proved.
issues.why_classification: The old proof uses the false two-dimensional embedding H² into W^{1,∞}, so a genuine mathematical repair is required. The excluded H² class at the advertised α=1 endpoint is natural and substantial enough that the change is not merely a minor technical qualification. Nevertheless, the proof alteration is local and the strict regularity strengthening is limited, leaving a recognizably comparable spectral theorem.

issues.title: Unjustified N-uniform IFRK4 local error

failure_location.quote: Under the regularity assumption, the constant in the $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^5)$ term is bounded uniformly in $N$, completing the proof of the local error estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: In the transformed vector field F(t,V)=e^{-Lt}N(e^{Lt}V), the diagonal multiplier L has spatial order 1+α. The fifth-order RK4 remainder involves vector-field derivatives through order four, and explicit time differentiations introduce powers of L in addition to the derivative in the quadratic nonlinearity. The old proof writes formal Taylor expansions but never bounds these terms uniformly in N or connects the stated exact-solution regularity to uniform semidiscrete trajectory and stage bounds. Smoothness in each finite-dimensional system therefore supports only a fixed-N remainder, not the asserted uniform constant.
issues.overall_effect: The old source does not establish an N-independent O(Δt^5) one-step defect, so that estimate cannot serve as a uniform premise for a fully discrete convergence bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the one-step defect using the exact transformed semi-discrete flow and state explicit N-uniform high-Sobolev bounds for that flow and the RK4 stages. A concrete sufficient assumption is q>4(1+α)+5. Use the unitarity of e^{Lt}, the order 1+α of L, and Sobolev product estimates to bound all vector-field derivatives and elementary differentials required through RK4 order four independently of N. The RK4 order conditions and a fifth-order integral remainder then yield ‖τ_{n+1}‖≤CΔt^5 with an N-independent C.
issues.why_classification: Smoothness of each finite-dimensional ODE gives only a fixed-N remainder because explicit time derivatives introduce powers of the unbounded multiplier L. Establishing uniformity requires substantial derivative counting, stage estimates, and stronger finite regularity assumptions. This is a contained local-consistency argument that retains the same uniform fifth-order defect in a comparable smooth regime, so it is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Unsupported nonlinear accumulation to fourth-order global error

failure_location.quote: The global error accumulates as $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^4)$ over $\mathcal{O}(1/\Delta t)$ time steps.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims fourth-order global temporal convergence, and consequently the fully discrete bound C_1N^{-r}+C_2Δt^4 with constants independent of N and Δt. The old paper actually provides only a claimed one-step local defect and a stability theorem for a linearized equation. It gives no estimate comparing two nonlinear semidiscrete flows, especially flows issued from computed values. Thus local consistency and linearized stability do not support the claimed nonlinear global convergence; an N-independent error-propagation bound is the material missing step.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised global fourth-order temporal rate and the resulting fully discrete spatial-temporal error bound are unsupported in the old version.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State explicit N- and Δt-independent high-Sobolev bounds for both the exact semi-discrete trajectory and the one-step exact semi-discrete flows issued from the computed values. Prove nonlinear L² flow stability under those bounds by comparing two semi-discrete solutions and obtaining ‖S_N(t_{n+1};t_n,Z)-S_N(t_{n+1};t_n,W)‖≤e^{CΔt}‖Z-W‖. Combining this with a valid uniform one-step defect gives the recurrence e_{n+1}≤e^{CΔt}e_n+CΔt^5; discrete Grönwall yields e_n≤CΔt^4, which may then be combined with the spatial estimate by the triangle inequality.
issues.why_classification: The linearized stability theorem does not control perturbations between nonlinear trajectories, especially trajectories starting from computed data. A nonlinear flow-stability lemma, uniform regularity regime, and discrete error-propagation argument are therefore genuinely missing. These additions are nontrivial but remain contained within the temporal analysis and preserve the fourth-order and combined rates under a recognizably comparable smooth, stable regime.
